1	/**
2	 * Runtime globals a declared Node core module needs when a browser evaluates it.
3	 *
4	 * Declaring a node-core module for a browser bundle — the mechanism
5	 * {@link declareUndeclaredRuntimeDependencies} and its siblings use when a
6	 * published library's own code reaches for `util`, `path` or their kin — closes
7	 * the *resolution* hole. It does not close the *evaluation* hole. The published
8	 * browser implementation of a core module is still a module written against
9	 * Node's runtime surface, and the parts of that surface it touches while it is
10	 * being evaluated have to exist before the first byte of it runs. `util@0.12.5`
11	 * reads `process.env.NODE_DEBUG` at its top level; in a browser, with nothing
12	 * named `process`, that read is a `ReferenceError` and the bundle throws before
13	 * the application's own code is reached.
14	 *
15	 * A bundler that shimmed every Node global would close that hole and a hundred
16	 * holes nobody has, and would ship the closure of `process`, `Buffer`, `timers`
17	 * and their transitive dependencies into a browser bundle to answer a single
18	 * property read. This capability refuses that trade. What it supplies is
19	 * derived from the installed module's own bytes and nothing else:
20	 *
21	 * - **Only what evaluation reaches.** A reference that sits inside a function
22	 *   body is not evaluated when the module is evaluated, and a reference under
23	 *   `typeof` cannot throw. Neither proves a need, so neither earns a shim, and
24	 *   the global is refused by name with that reason.
25	 * - **Only the shape the reading spells.** The shim materialises exactly the
26	 *   objects a proven dereference path walks through — `process` and
27	 *   `process.env` for `process.env.NODE_DEBUG`, and nothing else. The leaf is
28	 *   never invented: reading it yields `undefined`, which is what a browser
29	 *   process-less environment honestly has.
30	 * - **Only reads.** A global reached at evaluation time in a way an object
31	 *   graph cannot satisfy — called, constructed, assigned to, or reached through
32	 *   a computed member whose key is not in the source — is refused by name
33	 *   rather than half-supplied. An empty object standing where a function is
34	 *   called is a different crash, not a fix.
35	 *
36	 * The names every conforming ECMAScript host binds, and the names a CommonJS
37	 * module wrapper binds, are not candidates at all: they are already there, in
38	 * every browser and in every bundle, and shimming them would be a claim about
39	 * the host rather than a reading of the module.
40	 *
41	 * The seam the shim is delivered through is the builder's own: the Angular
42	 * workspace's `polyfills` entry points, which the browser builder emits into a
43	 * bundle the document loads before `main`. Nothing here writes a bundler alias,
44	 * a `define` substitution or a global variable injection plugin; the shim is an
45	 * ordinary module of the application, visible in the workspace and in the
46	 * emitted output like any other.
47	 */
48	
49	import { compareStrings } from './angular-target-cell.ts';
50	import {
51		objectAt,
52		parseStrictJson,
53		serializeJson,
54		type ConfigChange,
55		type JsonObject,
56	} from './angular-workspace-migration.ts';
57	import { lineOf, parseModule, type AstNode } from './semantic-module.ts';
58	import type { InstalledFile } from './undeclared-runtime-dependency.ts';
59	
60	const CAPABILITY = 'Node core runtime globals';
61	
62	/**
63	 * The value properties of the ECMAScript global object.
64	 *
65	 * Definitional rather than curated: every conforming host binds these, which is
66	 * what "conforming" means, so a reference to one says nothing about a global the
67	 * browser is missing.
68	 */

70		[

73			'ArrayBuffer',
74			'BigInt',

76			'BigUint64Array',
77			'Boolean',

82			'FinalizationRegistry',
83			'Float32Array',
84			'Float64Array',
85			'Function',
86			'Infinity',
87			'Int16Array',
88			'Int32Array',
89			'Int8Array',
90			'Intl',
91			'JSON',
92			'Map',
93			'Math',
94			'NaN',
95			'Number',
96			'Object',
97			'Promise',
98			'Proxy',
99			'RangeError',
100			'ReferenceError',
101			'Reflect',
102			'RegExp',
103			'Set',
104			'SharedArrayBuffer',
105			'String',
106			'Symbol',
107			'SyntaxError',
108			'TypeError',
109			'URIError',

111			'Uint32Array',

117			'decodeURI',

132	 * Names outside ECMAScript that a browser binds anyway.
133	 *
134	 * Every entry is a global the HTML standard or a WHATWG standard obliges a
135	 * browsing context to have, and which Node also binds — which is why a module
136	 * written for Node reaches for one. Supplying any of these would be a claim
137	 * about the browser, not a reading of the module, so they are excluded from
138	 * candidacy instead. The list is deliberately confined to the names a Node core
139	 * module's browser implementation plausibly touches; a name outside it is not
140	 * assumed absent either, it is refused by name and reported, which is a
141	 * diagnosable outcome rather than a silent one.
142	 */
143	export const WEB_PLATFORM_GLOBAL_NAMES: readonly string[] = Object.freeze(
144		[
145			'AbortController',
146			'AbortSignal',
147			'Blob',
148			'ByteLengthQueuingStrategy',
149			'CompressionStream',
150			'CountQueuingStrategy',
151			'DecompressionStream',
152			'DOMException',
153			'Event',
154			'EventTarget',
155			'Headers',
156			'MessageChannel',
157			'MessageEvent',
158			'MessagePort',
159			'ReadableStream',
160			'Request',
161			'Response',
162			'TextDecoder',
163			'TextEncoder',
164			'TransformStream',
165			'URL',
166			'URLSearchParams',
167			'WebAssembly',
168			'WritableStream',
169			'atob',
170			'btoa',
171			'clearInterval',
172			'clearTimeout',
173			'console',
174			'crypto',
175			'fetch',
176			'performance',
177			'queueMicrotask',
178			'setInterval',
179			'setTimeout',
180			'structuredClone',
181		].sort(compareStrings),
182	);
183	
184	/**
185	 * The names a CommonJS module wrapper binds around a module's body, plus
186	 * `arguments`, which every non-arrow function binds.
187	 *
188	 * A bundler that resolved `require('util')` at all is a bundler that supplies
189	 * these, because otherwise the module it just resolved could not export
190	 * anything.
191	 */
192	export const COMMONJS_WRAPPER_NAMES: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
193		'__dirname',
194		'__filename',
195		'arguments',
196		'exports',
197		'module',
198		'require',
199	]);
200	
201	/**
202	 * Every name a reference to which proves nothing about a missing runtime
203	 * global, and so is never a candidate for a shim.
204	 */
205	export const HOST_PROVIDED_GLOBAL_NAMES: readonly string[] = Object.freeze(
206		[...ECMASCRIPT_GLOBAL_NAMES, ...WEB_PLATFORM_GLOBAL_NAMES, ...COMMONJS_WRAPPER_NAMES].sort(
207			compareStrings,
208		),
209	);
210	
211	const HOST_PROVIDED: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(HOST_PROVIDED_GLOBAL_NAMES);
212	
213	/** Scope kinds whose body is not evaluated when the module is evaluated. */
214	const DEFERRED_SCOPE_KINDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
215		'class',
216		'function',
217		'functionBody',
218		'staticBlock',
219	]);
220	
221	/** One dereference of a runtime global the module performs while it is evaluated. */
222	export type RuntimeGlobalDereference = Readonly<{
223		/** The installed file the read was found in. */
224		file: string;
225		/** The 1-based line the read sits on. */
226		line: number;
227		/** The property names walked off the global, outermost first. */
228		path: readonly string[];
229	}>;
230	
231	/** A runtime global the reading proves the module dereferences at evaluation. */
232	export type ProvenRuntimeGlobal = Readonly<{
233		name: string;
234		/**
235		 * The dotted paths the shim has to materialise as objects, shortest first:
236		 * the global itself, and every intermediate a proven path walks through.
237		 */
238		containers: readonly string[];
239		dereferences: readonly RuntimeGlobalDereference[];
240	}>;
241	
242	/** What one installed module's evaluation asks of the runtime, as read. */
243	export type RuntimeGlobalReading = Readonly<{
244		proven: readonly ProvenRuntimeGlobal[];
245		/** Globals the reading found and refused, one sentence each, named. */
246		refused: readonly string[];
247	}>;
248	
249	/** The installed node-core module a browser bundle declares, as read from disk. */
250	export type NodeCoreModuleDeclaration = Readonly<{
251		/** The declared package name, e.g. `util`. */
252		module: string;
253		/** The installed version, for the record rather than for a decision. */
254		version: string;
255		/** The declared range in the application manifest, for the record. */
256		range: string;
257		/** The files a browser evaluates when it resolves the module. */
258		files: readonly InstalledFile[];
259	}>;
260	
261	export type NodeCoreRuntimeGlobals = Readonly<{
262		module: string;
263		version: string;
264		/** The globals supplied, in the order the shim writes them. */
265		globals: readonly ProvenRuntimeGlobal[];
266		/** The shim module's source, or null when the reading proved nothing. */
267		shim: string | null;
268		/** One line per assignment the shim makes. */
269		changes: readonly string[];
270		/** What supplying these globals changes about the application, declared. */
271		declaredDifferences: readonly string[];
272		/** Globals refused by name, and why. */
273		unhandled: readonly string[];
274	}>;
275	
276	function scopeIsEvaluatedAtLoad(scope: { kind: string; parent: unknown } | null): boolean {
277		let current = scope;
278		while (current !== null) {
279			if (DEFERRED_SCOPE_KINDS.has(current.kind)) return false;
280			current = (current as { parent: { kind: string; parent: unknown } | null }).parent;
281		}
282		return true;
283	}
284	
285	type ChainReading =
286		| Readonly<{ kind: 'path'; path: readonly string[] }>
287		| Readonly<{ kind: 'refused'; why: string }>;
288	
289	/**
290	 * The property path a reference walks off its global, or the reason no object
291	 * graph can stand in for it.
292	 *
293	 * The walk is deliberately syntactic and deliberately shallow: it follows
294	 * non-computed member accesses upwards from the identifier and stops at the
295	 * first thing that is not one. What it stops at decides the answer — a
296	 * `CallExpression` whose callee is the chain means a function was wanted, a
297	 * `NewExpression` means a constructor was, an assignment target means the
298	 * module writes through the global, and a computed member means the key is not
299	 * in the source to be read.
300	 */
301	function readDereferenceChain(
302		module: ReturnType<typeof parseModule>,
303		node: AstNode,
304	): ChainReading {
305		const path: string[] = [];
306		let current = node;
307		for (;;) {
308			const parent = module.parentOf(current);
309			if (parent === null)
310				return { kind: 'refused', why: 'it is evaluated as a bare value with no member read' };
311			if (parent.type === 'MemberExpression' && parent.object === current) {
312				if (parent.computed === true)
313					return {
314						kind: 'refused',
315						why: 'it is reached through a computed member, whose key the source does not state',
316					};
317				const property = parent.property as AstNode;
318				if (property.type !== 'Identifier')
319					return {
320						kind: 'refused',
321						why: 'it is reached through a member this reading cannot name',
322					};
323				path.push(property.name as string);
324				current = parent;
325				continue;
326			}
327			if (
328				(parent.type === 'CallExpression' || parent.type === 'NewExpression') &&
329				parent.callee === current
330			)
331				return {
332					kind: 'refused',
333					why:
334						path.length === 0
335							? 'it is called at module evaluation, and an object graph is not a function'
336							: `its member ${path.join('.')} is called at module evaluation, and an object ` +
337								'graph supplies no function to call',
338				};
339			if (parent.type === 'AssignmentExpression' && parent.left === current)
340				return { kind: 'refused', why: 'the module assigns through it at evaluation' };
341			if (parent.type === 'UpdateExpression' && parent.argument === current)
342				return { kind: 'refused', why: 'the module updates through it at evaluation' };
343			if (path.length === 0)
344				return { kind: 'refused', why: 'it is evaluated as a bare value with no member read' };
345			return { kind: 'path', path: Object.freeze([...path]) };
346		}
347	}
348	
349	/** Whether a reference sits directly under `typeof`, where nothing can throw. */
350	function isTypeofOperand(module: ReturnType<typeof parseModule>, node: AstNode): boolean {
351		const parent = module.parentOf(node);
352		return parent !== null && parent.type === 'UnaryExpression' && parent.operator === 'typeof';
353	}
354	
355	/**
356	 * Read every runtime global one installed module's evaluation requires.
357	 *
358	 * The unit of proof is the reference, and every reference of every candidate
359	 * name is classified: proven when the module dereferences it at load with a
360	 * member path an object graph can satisfy, refused otherwise. A name with even
361	 * one refused evaluation-time reach is refused entirely, because a shim that
362	 * answers the read and not the call would move the crash rather than remove it.
363	 */
364	export function readRuntimeGlobalReferences(
365		files: readonly InstalledFile[],
366	): RuntimeGlobalReading {
367		const dereferences = new Map<string, RuntimeGlobalDereference[]>();
368		const deferred = new Set<string>();
369		const hardRefusals = new Map<string, string>();
370		for (const file of files) {
371			const module = parseModule(CAPABILITY, file.path, file.source);
372			for (const reference of module.unresolvedReferences) {
373				const name = reference.name;
374				if (HOST_PROVIDED.has(name)) continue;
375				if (reference.inTypePosition) continue;
376				const node = reference.node as unknown as AstNode;
377				if (isTypeofOperand(module, node)) {
378					deferred.add(name);
379					continue;
380				}
381				if (!scopeIsEvaluatedAtLoad(reference.scope as unknown as { kind: string; parent: unknown })) {
382					deferred.add(name);
383					continue;
384				}
385				if (reference.isWrite) {
386					if (!hardRefusals.has(name))
387						hardRefusals.set(name, 'the module assigns to it at evaluation');
388					continue;
389				}
390				const chain = readDereferenceChain(module, node);
391				if (chain.kind === 'refused') {
392					if (!hardRefusals.has(name)) hardRefusals.set(name, chain.why);
393					continue;
394				}
395				const list = dereferences.get(name) ?? [];
396				list.push(
397					Object.freeze({
398						file: file.path,
399						line: lineOf(file.source, node.start),
400						path: chain.path,
401					}),
402				);
403				dereferences.set(name, list);
404			}
405		}
406		const proven: ProvenRuntimeGlobal[] = [];
407		const refused: string[] = [];
408		for (const name of [...dereferences.keys()].sort(compareStrings)) {
409			const reads = dereferences.get(name) ?? [];
410			const hard = hardRefusals.get(name);
411			if (hard !== undefined) {
412				refused.push(
413					`${name} is dereferenced at module evaluation, but ${hard}, so no shim this ` +
414						'capability can write would answer it and none was written',
415				);
416				continue;
417			}
418			const containers = new Set<string>([name]);
419			for (const read of reads)
420				for (let depth = 1; depth < read.path.length; depth += 1)
421					containers.add([name, ...read.path.slice(0, depth)].join('.'));
422			proven.push(
423				Object.freeze({
424					name,
425					containers: Object.freeze(
426						[...containers].sort(
427							(left, right) => left.split('.').length - right.split('.').length ||
428								compareStrings(left, right),
429						),
430					),
431					dereferences: Object.freeze(
432						[...reads].sort(
433							(left, right) =>
434								compareStrings(left.file, right.file) || left.line - right.line,
435						),
436					),
437				}),
438			);
439		}
440		for (const name of [...hardRefusals.keys()].sort(compareStrings))
441			if (!dereferences.has(name))
442				refused.push(
443					`${name} is reached at module evaluation, but ${hardRefusals.get(name) ?? ''}, so no ` +
444						'shim this capability can write would answer it and none was written',
445				);
446		for (const name of [...deferred].sort(compareStrings)) {
447			if (dereferences.has(name) || hardRefusals.has(name)) continue;
448			refused.push(
449				`${name} is referenced by this module, but every reference to it is inside a function ` +
450					'body or under `typeof`, neither of which runs — or can throw — when the module is ' +
451					'evaluated. The reading does not prove it is needed, so it is not supplied',
452			);
453		}
454		return Object.freeze({ proven: Object.freeze(proven), refused: Object.freeze(refused) });
455	}
456	
457	/** The TypeScript expression that reaches one container path off `globalThis`. */
458	function containerAccess(path: string): string {
459		const segments = path.split('.');
460		let expression = 'runtimeGlobals';
461		for (const segment of segments.slice(0, -1))
462			expression = `(${expression}[${JSON.stringify(segment)}] as RuntimeGlobalObject)`;
463		return `${expression}[${JSON.stringify(segments[segments.length - 1] as string)}]`;
464	}
465	
466	/**
467	 * Supply the runtime globals one declared node-core module's browser evaluation
468	 * requires, as an ordinary polyfill module of the application.
469	 *
470	 * Nothing is supplied that the reading did not prove, and nothing proven is
471	 * supplied more widely than the reading spells. A declaration whose module
472	 * dereferences no runtime global at evaluation gets no shim at all and no
473	 * entry point — which is the common case, and the case a blanket polyfill set
474	 * would have paid for anyway.
475	 */
476	export function supplyNodeCoreRuntimeGlobals(
477		declaration: NodeCoreModuleDeclaration,
478	): NodeCoreRuntimeGlobals {
479		const reading = readRuntimeGlobalReferences(declaration.files);
480		const label = `${declaration.module}@${declaration.version}`;
481		if (reading.proven.length === 0)
482			return Object.freeze({
483				module: declaration.module,
484				version: declaration.version,
485				globals: Object.freeze([]),
486				shim: null,
487				changes: Object.freeze([]),
488				declaredDifferences: Object.freeze([]),
489				unhandled: Object.freeze([...reading.refused]),
490			});
491		const changes: string[] = [];
492		const lines: string[] = [
493			'/**',
494			` * Runtime globals ${label} dereferences while a browser evaluates it.`,
495			' *',
496			` * Declared for this application because ${declaration.module} is in its declared`,
497			` * closure at ${declaration.range} as the browser implementation of a Node core`,
498			' * module, and a browser binds none of the names below. Every assignment here is a',
499			" * read of the installed module's own bytes, cited by file and line; nothing is",
500			' * supplied that no line asks for, and every leaf is left undefined rather than',
501			' * invented.',
502			' *',
503			' * Generated by @versionless/angular (node-core-runtime-globals).',
504			' */',
505			'',
506			'type RuntimeGlobalObject = Record<string, unknown>;',
507			'',
508			'const runtimeGlobals = globalThis as unknown as RuntimeGlobalObject;',
509			'',
510		];
511		for (const global of reading.proven) {
512			for (const read of global.dereferences)
513				lines.push(
514					`// ${global.name}.${read.path.join('.')} — ${read.file} line ${String(read.line)}`,
515				);
516			for (const container of global.containers) {
517				lines.push(`${containerAccess(container)} ??= {};`);
518				changes.push(`${container} supplied as an empty object when the host binds nothing there`);
519			}
520			lines.push('');
521		}
522		lines.push('export {};', '');
523		const declaredDifferences = reading.proven.map(
524			(global) =>
525				`globalThis.${global.name} exists in this application's browser context where it did ` +
526				`not before, as ${global.containers.length === 1 ? 'an empty object' : `the object graph ${global.containers.join(', ')}`}. ` +
